text: When I told him quietly that I was the captain, the swimmer, after a pause, gave his name as Leggatt and climbed aboard, and I hurried below to fetch him a sleeping suit. <break time="0.8s" /> Dressed in grey stripes exactly like my own, he stood beside me in the dark, and it seemed to me that I was looking at my double, my second self, risen out of the sea. <break time="0.8s" /> He had been chief mate of the Sephora, the ship anchored inside the islands, and during a terrible gale he had quarrelled with an insolent sailor who refused to obey his orders. <break time="0.8s" /> At the height of the storm he set a reefed foresail that saved the ship, yet in the struggle a huge sea fell upon them, and when the two men were found, the sailor was dead. <break time="0.8s" /> Shut up in his cabin for weeks by his captain, he expected to be handed over to the law at the first port and to be tried for the death on shore. <break time="0.8s" /> Finding his door unlocked one evening, he had slipped into the sea and swum to the islands, and from there, seeing my riding light, he had made for it, resolved never to go back. <break time="0.8s" /> Not for a moment did I think of calling my officers, for something in his calm, low voice made me feel that his trouble might, in other circumstances, have been mine. <break time="0.8s" /> So I led him to my stateroom, an L shaped room whose inner part could not be seen from the door, and there, side by side, we whispered in the dark.
